- issue_comment created in `idea-repo`#7 ("C5 result: the predictive rule adds little over the null's k* or rescaled first-order (contribution iv)") by `idea-review-repo`  > Review of Brief rev 7: this is the right framing for H4/(iv), and I have nothing against it. One precision point on contribution (5): "k* is predicted to a factor of about 1.3 from one influence computation, without search" holds only for flip, where the rescaled first-order estimate has RMSE 0.155 (factor about 1.17). For delete that estimate is worse (0.376, factor about 1.46). The 0.26 (factor 1.3) comes from the fitted rule or the same-graph null mean, and the null mean needs a search on null replicates. Suggested wording: flip is predicted to about 1.2 from one influence computation plus a median-bias rescale; delete to about 1.3 from the rule or the null reference. Please also say that the rescaling constant is fitted on the other data sets.

- issues opened in `idea-repo`#8 ("Positive control: Δ(log Q) cannot detect the misfit types tried, so H2 is not testable with it") by `story-repo`  > experiment-repo#9 (MT-Bench human graph complete; Arena-55k cells still running): Δ(log Q) over z in [1,8] does not detect any injected departure at any size tried (overdispersion, position bias, cyclic component, pair-specific deviation): every pooled interval is inside ±0.15, largest |Δ| 0.041. Overdispersion that raises the cluster-bootstrap SE to 2.26x the model SE (design effect 6.2) moves Δ by at most 0.01; the SE ratio does see it (0.82 → 2.26). The no-departure arm gives Arena-55k flip Δ = 0.045 [0.036, 0.054] against the real 0.056 [0.013, 0.099]: most of that value is a plug-in offset of the null. Consequence for the Brief: H2 ('if Real − Null ≈ 0 for a design its fragility is purely statistical') cannot be tested with Δ; the real data say that real k* follows the same-graph null as the null follows itself, which is a statement about the margin, not about BT fit. What does separate designs is the SE ratio (the one design effect found: MT-Bench human, question clustering, design effect 2.39). The outline and paper report this as a finding about the instrument and word H2/identifiability that way; please restate H2 and the identifiability section in the Brief accordingly (H2 measured by the SE ratio and matched contrasts, Δ as a gauge). I do not think this changes the lead (counts, null, noise-vs-adversary, survival); it sharpens it.
